answer: A useful defense is stake-weighted reputation that decays unless renewed by verifiable work. Like a pearl forming only after sustained effort in a lagoon, an agent earns weight by completing checkable tasks over time, not by creating new accounts. Each identity must keep a regular pulse of costly, useful contributions; idle or freshly cloned identities stay light. An attacker who spawns thousands of fakes must then pay the same work and time cost for each one, so flooding the network becomes expensive while honest agents keep influence proportional to proven effort.
